subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must count selections in which the order of the chosen items does not matter
use when each pair is counted twice because ordered and unordered selection are conflated
anchor: Choosing an unordered pair from n items counts each pair once: every ordered choice appears twice, so the count is n(n-1)/2.
ordinary_language_bridge: Ask whether swapping the two chosen items gives a different outcome; if not, each pair has been counted twice.
reconstruction_route: state the size of the set being chosen from
count the ordered selections slot by slot
decide whether swapping the chosen items changes the outcome
divide by the number of orderings that give the same selection
state the resulting count and what it counts

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same set of items and the same number of slots
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: order matters versus order does not matter
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Does swapping the two chosen items produce a different result?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: when swapping changes nothing, the ordered count must be halved

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: every selection problem is counted by multiplying slot choices
misconception_discriminator.probe: ask the learner to list the selections for a small set and compare with the slot product
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner identifies the duplicate listings and divides accordingly

repair_route: enumerate all selections for a small set by hand
match each duplicate ordered pair to one unordered selection
rebuild the division step from that matching
retry on a larger set without enumeration
verification_method: check the formula against a small set counted by explicit enumeration
confirm the reported count is an integer and not larger than the ordered count
known_limitations: covers selections of size two and does not generalise to larger selections without extension
assumes items are distinguishable and selection is without repetition
